root_cause.text: The s390 BPF JIT failed to zero-extend unsigned return values and kfunc arguments as required by the s390x ABI, only performing sign extension, which can cause incorrect value propagation and potential security issues.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "s390x ABI requires callers to zero-extend unsigned arguments and sign-extend signed arguments, and callees to zero-extend unsigned return values and sign-extend signed return values. s390 BPF JIT currently implements only sign extension." The patch renames `sign_extend` to `sign_zero_extend` and adds conditional emission of zero-extension instructions (llgcr, llghr, llgfr) when the `BTF_FMODEL_SIGNED_ARG` flag is not set, confirming the missing zero-extension logic.

The patch renames `sign_extend` to `sign_zero_extend` and adds conditional emission of zero-extension instructions (llgcr, llghr, llgfr) when the `BTF_FMODEL_SIGNED_ARG` flag is not set, confirming the missing zero-extension logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add zero-extension support for unsigned arguments in BPF JIT sign/zero extension helper, fixing incorrect handling of unsigned function arguments.
intent_record.what: Renamed function `sign_extend` to `sign_zero_extend` and modified it to emit zero-extension instructions for unsigned arguments (when `BTF_FMODEL_SIGNED_ARG` not set) for sizes 1, 2, and 4, in addition to existing sign-extension instructions for signed arguments.
intent_record.how: Now, when an argument is unsigned, the JIT compiler emits the appropriate zero-extend instruction (llgcr, llghr, llgfr) instead of performing no extension, ensuring that upper bits of the register are cleared to zero for narrower unsigned values.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace sign extension with zero extension for function call arguments in BPF JIT compiler to correctly handle unsigned or size-specific argument types.
intent_record.what: Changed function call from sign_extend to sign_zero_extend when extending arguments of BPF function calls in the JIT compiler.
intent_record.how: This switch from sign extension to zero extension modifies how argument values are sized to full register width: previously, smaller arguments were sign-extended (filling higher bits with the sign bit), now they are zero-extended (filling higher bits with zeros).

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace sign_extend with sign_zero_extend to correctly handle both sign and zero extension of return values based on return flags in BPF trampoline JIT.
intent_record.what: Changed function call from sign_extend to sign_zero_extend for extending the return value in invoke_bpf_prog.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes the emitted extension instruction from sign-only extension to one that respects m->ret_flags, allowing both sign and zero extension as needed.

The group directly addresses the root cause by replacing sign extension with sign/zero extension for return values, which is exactly the fix needed for the missing zero-extension of unsigned values in s390 BPF JIT.

This call to sign_extend performs only sign extension for function arguments, leaving unsigned arguments unextended.
This call to sign_extend performs only sign extension for the return value, failing to zero-extend unsigned returns.
